drivingQuestion: How to reconcile the two baraitot on moving hay between fine- and foul-mouthed animals
outcomeNote: contradiction resolved by reading both baraitot as donkey-to-ox

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מִקַּמֵּי חַמְרָא לְקַמֵּי תוֹרָא — שָׁקְלִינַן, מִקַּמֵּי תוֹרָא לְקַמֵּי חַמְרָא — לָא שָׁקְלִינַן. וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי ״נוֹטֵל מִלִּפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה שֶׁפִּיהָ יָפֶה״ — בַּחֲמוֹר, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ רִירֵי. ״וְנוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה שֶׁפִּיהָ רַע״ — בְּפָרָה,
segments.en: «Abaye said:» Both «this» baraita «and that» baraita hold that «one may take» hay «from before a donkey» and place it «before an ox.» However, «one may not take» hay «from before an ox» and place it «before a donkey.» The formulation of the baraitot can be explained as follows: «That which was taught: One may take» hay «from before an animal whose mouth is fine,» is referring to «a donkey,» and the reason the baraita says its mouth is fine is «because it has no spittle.» Therefore, the donkey does not dampen the remaining hay with its saliva. «And» the statement: «And one may place it before an animal whose mouth is foul,» is referring to «a cow,»

segments.he: וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי ״נוֹטְלִין מִלִּפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה שֶׁפִּיהָ רַע״ — בַּחֲמוֹר, דְּלָא דָּיֵיק וְאָכֵיל. ״וְנוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה שֶׁפִּיהָ יָפֶה״ — בְּפָרָה, דְּדָיְיקָא וְאָכְלָה.
segments.en: «And that which was taught» in the other baraita: «One may take» hay «from before an animal whose mouth is foul,» is referring to «a donkey.» Its mouth is foul «because it does not discern» between different foods «and» it «eats» everything. «And» the statement: «One may place it before an animal whose mouth is fine,» is referring «to a cow, which discerns» between different foods «and» only then «it eats.»

moves.summary: both baraitot: donkey to ox, not ox to donkey
moves.about: both baraitot allow moving hay from a donkey to an ox but not the reverse
